slide.heading: More concentrated does not mean faster particles
slide.lead: Both acids are at 20 °C. Their particles have the same average kinetic energy.

points.label: What changes
points.text: More particles occupy the same volume.

points.label: Why rate rises
points.text: More successful collisions occur each second.

figure.shows: Two equal-volume acid panels beside identical magnesium surfaces. One has fewer particles and one has more. Representative motion arrows have the same length in both panels, showing that concentration alone does not increase average particle speed.
